sections.title: Ways of speaking
sections.content:
How people communicate differently:
• articulate — expressing ideas clearly. She's remarkably articulate for her age.
• concise — using few words effectively. Keep your presentation concise and to the point.
• vague — unclear or imprecise. His instructions were too vague to follow.
• blunt — direct and honest to the point of rudeness. She can be quite blunt in her feedback.
• eloquent — fluent and persuasive in speech. The president delivered an eloquent speech on equality.

sections.title: Written communication
sections.content:
Terms for different types of writing:
• coherent — logical and consistent. The essay needs to be more coherent in its argument.
• ambiguous — open to more than one interpretation. The contract language was ambiguous and caused disputes.
• succinct — briefly and clearly expressed. Please provide a succinct summary of the report.
• verbose — using more words than needed. Academic writing should be precise, not verbose.
• compelling — convincing and persuasive. She wrote a compelling argument for change.

exercises.question: Someone who expresses ideas very clearly is:
exercises.explanation: Articulate means able to express thoughts clearly and effectively.

exercises.question: Writing that uses too many unnecessary words is:
exercises.hint: They could say it in fewer words.
exercises.explanation: Verbose means using more words than are needed.

exercises.question: A message that could mean different things is:
exercises.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation.

exercises.question: An argument that is logical and makes sense is:
Very direct honesty that might seem rude is being:
A speech that is beautiful and persuasive is:
exercises.explanation: Eloquent means fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing.

exercises.question: Expressing something briefly and clearly is being:
An argument so powerful it's hard to resist is:
exercises.explanation: Compelling means evoking interest or attention in a powerfully irresistible way.
